Fantasy football DST strategy is usually to try to find a group that: -Is cheap enough to wait until the last round or two -Has an opening schedule that can get us through 4+ weeks -Has some blue-chip talents/could be really good in real life Top-three candidates: -Chargers (ADP DST10): Start the season with ARI and LV before a tough stretch. Lost Jesse Minter but would like to think they'll keep things similar schematically (if it ain't broke, don't fix it). Still have Derwin James holding things down. -Ravens (DST11): Get IND, NO, DAL (not good), TEN, ATL, CLE in the first six weeks. Should be decent favorites in each game? Added Jesse Minter, got their stud EDGE in Trey Hendrickson, and still have Kyle Hamilton to be the ultimate chess piece. Definitely my favorite target. -Lions (DST18): NO, BUF (not good), NYJ, CAR, ARI before their Week 6 bye. Should be pretty solid favorites in 4/5 games. Maybe the injury gods chill out for once? Wouldn't be surprised if Aidan Hutchinson makes a leap and flirts with a 20-sack season one of these years.

ESPN story, via @mikecwright on Victor Wembanyama signing a $252 maximum extension with the San Antonio Spurs while deciding to potentially save the team roughly $50 million over the next five years: https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49328757/sources-spurs-victor-wembanyama-reach-252-million-max-extension

Spurs chairman Peter J. Holt, CEO RC Buford, GM Brian Wright and coach Mitch Johnson traveled to Paris to meet and spend time with Victor Wembanyama and his family and reps Friday. Wembanyama was essentially a lock to earn a $303M supermax if he played 65 games next season -- but he opted for a significant sacrifice at a flash point for the Spurs' rise. In the Spurs championship past, Tim Duncan, Manu Ginobili and Tony Parker had a history of taking less for the betterment of team-building.

Wembanyama decided on the 25% maximum instead of the 30% supermax escalators to $303M, after he and the Spurs went through multiple frameworks. A major decision for the All-NBA star and Defensive Player of the Year entering his fourth season. San Antonio worked in close partnership with Wembanyama and his representatives, offering the full super max and different variations of extensions. But Wembanyama ultimately chose a contract sacrifice rooted in giving him and the organization increased ability to build a sustained title contender around him.
BREAKING: San Antonio Spurs' Victor Wembanyama has signed a five-year, $252 million maximum rookie-scale contract extension, with a player option in the fifth season, sources tell ESPN.
